title: Cohortal drift & batch-entropy playbook: scheduler tuning notes
body:
Purpose and high-level:
This doc captures an informal experiment playbook and field notes for a class of scheduler behaviors we are calling ‘cohortal drift’ — when batches formed from dynamically changing request cohorts progressively skew latency and fairness metrics on long-lived workers. The goal is to surface small, reproducible knobs (batch size target, entropy-penalty, timeout anneal curve) that reduce p99/p999 without severe throughput loss for mixed workloads.

Context / motivation:
- Recent production trouble when a small subset of long-sequence chat requests causes local queue starvation and increases tail latency across tenants on the same worker.
- Existing continuous-batcher tunes primarily for average throughput; we need heuristics to detect cohort drift (i.e., persistent change in request length distribution or priority mix) and adapt flush rules.
- Want to produce a short list of practical guardrails to add to the scheduler: entropy-based acceptance limits, cohort aging penalty, timeout annealing, lightweight demotion.

Definitions (working):
- cohort: set of requests arriving within a short window that share key distribution features (seq_len bucket, priority tier, customer).
- entropy (batch-entropy): a simple measure of heterogeneity in sequence lengths and priority; higher entropy -> more heterogeneous -> higher risk of per-request slowdown if coalesced.
- cohortal drift: when the statistical properties of cohorts feeding a worker shift (e.g., more long-seq requests) and remain shifted for multiple scheduling intervals.

Hypotheses to test: (short form)
1) Adding an entropy penalty that reduces join probability for heterogeneous queues will lower p99 at <5% throughput cost.
2) Timeout annealing (start with short timeout, lengthen slowly when cohorts are stable) reduces starvation-driven spikes versus fixed timeouts.
3) Light demotion of continuity (move older cohorts into smaller micro-batches) improves fairness across priority classes.

Experiment matrix (primary factors):
- join_policy: baseline (first-come join), entropy-penalized, priority-weighted-join.
- batch_size_target: 4, 8, 16, 32 (per-worker logical slot).
- flush_timeout_ms: 6, 12, 25, 50, but also support exponential anneal (6->25 over 3 intervals).
- cohort_age_threshold_ms: 100, 500, 2000 (when to start demotion).
- cohort_entropy_threshold: 0.2, 0.5, 0.8 (normalized 0..1).
- demotion_fraction: 0.0, 0.25, 0.5 (fraction of batch to demote).
- workload mixes: steady short-only, mixed poisson (80/20 short/long), microburst (1s spike heavy long), diurnal synthetic replay (production trace sampled).

Metrics (instrumentation targets):
- latency percentiles per-request (p50, p90, p95, p99, p999) broken out by seq_len bucket and priority.
- throughput (tokens/sec) per worker and cluster-wide.
- batch composition stats: mean/median batch size, fraction homogeneous (>80% same-seq-bucket), entropy distribution per batch.
- starvation signals: number of requests delayed beyond 2x expected wait for target latency class.
- fairness index: per-tenant quantile gap metric (delta p95 between top- and bottom-decile tenants).
- GPU utilization, kernel hot-spot time, CPU scheduler time (host-side), and KV cache hit ratio.

Probing & workload harness:
- Use trace replayer (GHD-1234) to replay representative windows from Nov 2025 production capture; augment with synthetic microburst generator.
- Run single-worker microbench first (isolate variables), then scaled 16-worker cluster for amplification and multi-tenant interaction.
- Each config: 30 minutes warmup + 60 minutes measurement. Repeat 3 runs for variance.

Instrumentation checklist (must-have):
- enable microtraces for batch assembly path (annotate queue arrival, attempted-join, flush-trigger, kernel-launch).
- sample GPU / per-kernel timings at 100ms resolution.
- per-request metadata: seq_len, tenant_id_hash, priority, arrival_ts, enqueue_ts, dispatch_ts, finish_ts.
- add a small shim that computes batch-entropy at assembly time and exposes it to metrics.

Initial experiment plan (week 1 sprint):
- Day 1: synthetic smoke test to validate harness and metric hooks. Baseline run with current prod scheduler.
- Day 2–3: sweep entropy_penalty in isolation (no demotion, batch_size_target=16, timeout=25ms) across mixed-poisson workload.
- Day 4: run timeout-anneal vs fixed timeout on microburst workload.
- Day 5: combine best entropy_penalty + anneal, test demotion_fraction=0.25.

Early observations (notes-to-self from pilot runs):
- Pilot A (entropy-penalized join, penalty=0.3): p99 improved ~18% on mixed-poisson, throughput dropped ~3%. Qualitatively batches were smaller but more homogeneous.
- Pilot B (anneal 6->25ms over 3 intervals): in microburst case, anneal reduced starvation spikes but increased p50 slightly for short-only workload.
- Weird: when entropy threshold too low (0.2) we saw oscillations in batch size (frequent small batches) — causes CPU overhead that appears in kernel scheduling traces. Need hysteresis.

Failure modes to watch:
- Over-aggressive demotion causes many small kernel launches that amplify GPU kernel-launch overhead and reduces utilization — check kernel busy fraction.
- Entropy calculation cost: computing high-resolution entropy per candidate join can become CPU hot path; implement approximate streaming estimator or sample 10% of joins.
- Cross-tenant unfairness: naive demotion by cohort_age can preferentially slow new tenants; measure fairness index closely.

Low-effort mitigations we can ship quickly (if validated):
- 1) Entropy sample: compute batch-entropy using quantized seq_len buckets (4 buckets) to reduce compute cost.
- 2) Hysteresis window for entropy: require 2 consecutive intervals breaching threshold before penalizing joins.
- 3) Soft demotion: only demote low-priority cohort elements; keep high-priority in main batch.

Data artifacts to capture for review:
- histogram snapshots of batch_entropy over time (per worker).
- microtrace excerpts for top 10 p999 events and their batch compositions.
- workload replay job configs and seed files.

Open questions (research backlog):
- Is entropy the right metric or should we compute a cost-estimate that incorporates expected token-processing time per-request? (i.e., predicted kernel time).
- Can we use online learning to set anneal curves per-worker based on recent stability signals? (safe small model in Rust?).
- Interaction with KV cache: heterogeneous batches might reduce effective KV cache reuse; quantify via hit-rate delta.

Action items & owners: (short list)
- implement approximate batch-entropy shim (Maya) — target PR by 2026-01-15.
- run scale experiments with microburst harness (Arjun) — target 2026-01-22.
- add fairness metric dashboards and per-tenant p95 delta (Sofia) — target 2026-01-29.
- follow-up design doc proposing default anneal curves and hysteresis (Liam) — draft by 2026-02-05.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally rough: please read with an experimental mindset. The goal is to produce a small, incremental set of safe guardrails for the continuous-batcher rather than a large intrusive redesign.
- If you have prior experiments with similar entropy/heterogeneity heuristics (maybe from legacy coalescer work), paste links into the linked_artifacts or inline in comments.

Appendix: quick reproducible run command (local harness):
- ./replayer --trace traces/nov_captured_window.json --workers 1 --join-policy entropy --entropy-penalty 0.3 --batch-target 16 --timeout-anneal 6:25:3 --output metrics/run_entropy_pilot.json

End of doc.
